item.title: GTA 6 was the ‘biggest launch in PlayStation history’ with over 39 million players
item.summary: GTA 6 has broken another record
item.text:
Grand Theft Auto 6 was “the biggest launch in PlayStation history,” according to Sony, with over 39 million users playing the game on PS5.
According to a post on the PlayStation blog, players cumulatively logged 683 million hours of gameplay in GTA 6 between launch and November 22. The game also set a new record for concurrent players of a single game on PlayStation consoles.
PlayStation also claims that the platform holder “saw the largest number of newly connected PS5 consoles on a single day since the console’s launch, outside of end-of-year holidays.”
GTA 6 was also “the first game played on 70% of new PS5 consoles” during the period of launch until November 22.
This comes after Rockstar and publisher Take-Two announced that Grand Theft Auto 6 has become the most successful launch for any piece of media in history, after being pre-ordered over 32 million times.
On Friday, Rockstar and Take-Two claimed that the game has generated $3.79 billion in day one retail sales, “setting a new record for entertainment across any medium, and becoming the biggest entertainment launch in history.”
For comparison, Spider-Man: Brand New Day generated $2.5 billion across its entire theatrical run as the highest grossing film of the year. When compared to other GTA titles, GTA 5 generated $815 million on launch day, which means GTA 6 managed almost 5 times as much.
Grand Theft Auto 6 released on Thursday November 19, 13 years after the previous entry in the franchise. Upon release, the game achieved a record-tieing 99 out of 100 on Metacritic, making it one of the highest rated games of all time.
VGC’s Grand Theft Auto 6 review calls it “the game of the generation”, saying Rockstar “delivers its modern masterpiece with a remarkable artistic achievement that exceeds all expectations”.

item.title: The Last of Us 2 dev says "GTA 6 is the great pyramids of game development"
item.summary: "The sheer size of the script must be mind boggling"
item.text:
Welcome to a brand new week of GTA 6 still blowing everyone's minds. We will probably be covering this beat for months if not years as players and game developers continue unearthing new discoveries and technical marvels, with one prominent dev comparing GTA 6 to the Great Pyramids in Egypt.
Mark Richard Davies, game director at Naughty Dog and game designer on The Last of Us, is the latest game developer to appear awe-stricken in reaction to Rockstar's opus. A colleague of Davies, Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet world design director Michael Barclay, recently said GTA 6 appears to him "as a Bugatti Veyron would to a nervous Victorian child," underscoring the unprecedented depth and scale of the game.
In a new tweet, Davies says we might never find every piece of the GTA 6 puzzle and jokingly predicts we'll one day discover extraterrestrial intelligence hiding in its DNA. "GTA VI is the Great Pyramids of Game Development," he says. "As in, people will be asking for centuries how it was possible and we will eventually conclude that aliens made it."
In response to a commenter who rightfully points out Rockstar's "8 to 13" year development cycle and estimated $1 billion budget, Davis simply says, "I'm sure the pyramids were expensive too," seemingly acknowledging that one part of Rockstar's magic is unfathomable financial resources. For instance, the thing that amazes Davies the most about GTA 6, in his words, is that "Every NPC having voice lines and reactions. The sheer size of the script must be mind boggling." The level of interactivity and variety in GTA 6's NPCs is hugely immersive, but that wouldn't have been possible if Rockstar and parent company Take-Two Interactive didn't have the money to pay that amount of voice and performance capture artists.
All that said, in addition to unfathomable amounts of money, there's also an element to Rockstar's sterling track record for genre-defining releases that has very little to do with money and a lot to do with extremely talented individuals firing on all cylinders and a unified vision from legacy leadership. But, you know, having $1 billion dollars to spend certainly doesn't hurt.

item.title: GTA 6 Players Figure Out A Way To Remove Its Framerate Cap, But 60FPS Ain’t Happening Anytime Soon
item.summary: Rockstar has suggested not even the PS5 Pro could handle higher framerates in GTA 6
item.text:
60FPSGrand Theft Auto 6GTA 6Rockstar Games
A new glitch on Xbox lets players play Grand Theft Auto 6 without a framerate cap. It’s a neat trick that, in some circumstances, does allow the game to run at nearly 60FPS. However, this odd glitch really shows how GTA 6 is unlikely to get an actual performance mode anytime soon.
Grand Theft Auto 6 targets 30FPS on PlayStation 5 and Xbox. This performance limitation upset some players, especially those hoping the game would hit higher numbers on PS5 Pro. And in some areas of the game, it struggles to maintain that level of performance due to the immense amount of simulation happening under the hood and all the incredible visual effects running at all times. Rockstar has also explained that current-gen hardware can’t support higher framerates. That hasn’t stopped fans from trying, and a new Xbox bug has some claiming a 60FPS mode is here. But it’s more complicated than that.
As explained in a new video from Digital Foundry, this Xbox glitch, which was discovered by Reddit user Meowwie64 and involves tweaking some refresh settings while booting up GTA 6 and a second game, is fun to play around with, but isn’t a hidden high-performance mode.
After extensive testing, DF determined that playing GTA 6 with this glitch in effect resulted in an average framerate of 36FPS. That is higher than normal, but it doesn’t equate to a smoother experience. There are moments when you can get the game running at nearly 60FPS, but to do so you have to go out in the middle of the ocean, away from all the simulation and action, and look at the sky. And even then, GTA 6 can’t hit a locked 60FPS using this newly discovered glitch.
It also seems like this bug causes some weird issues with gameplay. When the framerate goes up, the game appears to speed up alongside it. This is likely a result of the bug and not a sign that GTA 6′s action is tied to the framerate. The one positive, as noted by Digital Foundry, is that input lag is reduced somewhat when using this mode. But keep in mind that as the framerate goes up, so does that game speed issue, making it harder to control the action while driving or shooting.
Some online have tried to claim this is some secret 60FPS mode that Rockstar has hidden in the game for… some reason. Or that Rockstar lied when it told Kotaku these consoles, even the PS5 Pro, can’t handle a 40 or 60FPS mode. But the truth is that this is just a weird bug that might get patched in the near future by Xbox or Rockstar

item.text:
It's impossible to have a big game launch these days without some section of the internet, somewhere, finding grievances with the final product because it does not align with the expectations they had pre-release.
The most recent upset comes in the form of Grand Theft Auto 6's revised take on, well, grand theft auto. In case you're one of the few still unfamiliar, grand theft auto is more than the titular moniker for Rockstar's premier crime simulation series; it's actually a US legal term for the act of stealing or attempting to steal a motor vehicle. In most previous GTA entries, this was a central part of the core gameplay loop: accept a mission, nick a car, complete the mission, nick another car, getaway. It's an endemic part of the loop, and has become so popular and identifiable as such that even other games - Watch Dogs, Saint's Row, Cyberpunk 2077, and so on - have emulated the mechanic.
So it makes sense that the internet is in a bit of a spin about GTA 6's more mature and restrained take on its eponymous crime. A quick, no-frills getaway in a vehicle you've hijacked on the road isn't always the most effective option. A mindless crime spree on the streets of Leonida is not a simple thing to pull off, nor an easy thing to live down. In this game, actions have consequences, and an ill-timed or ill-judged car jacking can quickly and efficiently put an end to your criminal ambitions.
That's not to say you cannot simply steal cars. Of course you can: the option to saunter up to an occupied vehicle and jack it from its registered owner is available to you from the very beginning of the game. But the citizens of Leonida aren't going to take your wanton act of foolishness lying down; many of the motorists in the county will fight back, pull a piece on you, or run you over mid-robbery attempt. Even if you are lucky to find one of the more pliant residents of the city, you might find something peculiar is happening in their car. I jacked a woman in the city over the weekend, and the cat she was ferrying from place to place decided to attack me, causing me to crash. item.title: Telegram CEO Says The ‘Least Realistic’ Thing About GTA 6 Is That Nobody Uses His App To Commit Crimes
item.summary: He just tweeted it out
item.text:
The lawyers for Pavel Durov have got to be going through it right now. The CEO of Telegram is one of the many millions of people who seem to be enjoying GTA 6. However, he has a few quibbles about the game’s realism. Late last week he posted on X, “The least realistic thing about GTA VI is that Jason and Lucia run a whole criminal operation without a single Telegram group.”
Telegram is a popular messaging app used worldwide. It functions similarly to Signal and allows for encrypted messaging, making it an attractive chat service for people who need to communicate privately including journalists, protestors, and labor organizers. Those features also make Telegram a hotspot for illegal activity.
Telegram has an infamous reputation for being the go-to app for crimes. Scratch some kind of criminal network of unsavory people like white nationalists or cryptoscammers, and you’re likely going to find a Telegram group chat. The app is so notorious for being Crime Facebook that in 2024 Durov was indicted in France on 12 charges for allegedly not doing enough to curb the drug trafficking and distribution of child sexual assault abuse materials taking place on Telegram. Earlier this year, Russia charged Durov with facilitating terrorism for failing to remove information allegedly used to target Russian soldiers, infrastructure, and civilians in the Russia-Ukraine war.
Durov has said Telegram actively works to remove illegal content from the app and has denied claims that it’s some kind of haven for criminals. Which is why it’s really weird that he’s salty-posting on X about how the two most famous fictional criminals in the world right now aren’t using his app to do their criming. He’s facing all this litigation for allegedly not doing enough about his app being the crime place and he just tweets an acknowledgement that he can’t even conceive of fictional crime being done without Telegram’s help.

item.title: GTA 6 hacker who leaked footage in 2022 has been released on licence and told not to do it again
item.summary: Arion Kurtaj was deemed to fit to stand trial earlier this year
item.text:
The UK teenager who hacked Rockstar and leaked footage of Grand Theft Auto 6 has been released on licence and warned not to do anything like it again.
In 2022, Arion Kurtaj, who suffers from acute autism, was convicted of being a member of the international hacking group Lapsus$, which also carried out attacks on tech companies including Uber, Nvidia and EE.
In late 2023, a judge determined that Kurtaj – who was 18 at the time – remained fixated with hacking and posed “a high risk of serious harm to the public through skill in gaining unfettered access to computers”.
It was decided that Kurtaj would stay at a secure hospital facility until such time that a mental health tribunal decided he no longer posed a danger to others.
Earlier this year, however, it was decided that he was now fit to stand trial, and was released to a normal prison in January.
The trial took place last week, where Kurtaj pleaded guilty. Now, as reported by the BBC, he has been given a Serious Crime Prevention Order, which restricts his online activity for the next five years, including a ban on using Telegram and Discord.
According to the report, the judge told Kurtaj that he was “a very talented young man”, and told him: “Don’t let this happen again.”
In September 2022, Kurtaj and other hackers published an hour of GTA 6 development footage online, giving players their first look at the sequel to one of the best-selling games of all-time.
This footage included the first look at Lucia, confirming for the first time that the game would feature a female protagonist.
At the time, Rockstar said it was “extremely disappointed” to have details on the game shared in this way, and proceeded to release the game’s first trailer later that year, officially confirming the female lead.

An unofficial GTA 6 PC release is in sight. GTA 6 leaker Cyberleek has released the executable file for the Xbox build of the game, which was shared earlier this month, formally firing the starting shot on recompilation work that could soon see Rockstar's game running on PC.
Users flagged the November 23 release of the Xbox EXE online. "The torch passes to the open source recomp and emulation projects. Before trusting any file, verify it," a message from Cyberleek reads.
Project Leonida is at the forefront of those recompilation efforts, pushing for a native GTA 6 version based on the leaked Xbox build. One of Leonida's lead developers, Shayder, reacted to the executable leak on Twitter: "CL has just dropped the exe, expect a lot of static recompilation work to be done soon."
Leonida is currently available to access online, with its creators noting it "does not contain the game, keys or an executable, and it does not explain how to get them. You need your own copy, with its files already readable on disk. Nothing here decrypts or works around any protection." You'll be shocked to hear the recomp is co-authored by Claude AI.
The release of this executable has not changed that, but it has kicked the GTA 6 PC race into high gear.
Just hours after the EXE arrived, an update went out to the Leonida Discord server: "The game almost boots. Black screen, audio cuts off."
After the news broke, the Leonida Discord server buckled under an influx of new users, forcing the moderators to end a live stream amid a temporary outage. The server was "not nuked," says one admin.

item.title: You Need to Watch GTA 6’s Telenovela Immediately

There is a ton of stuff to do in Grand Theft Auto 6. You can rob jewelry stores and steal exotic supercars. You can go scuba diving and hunt for pirate treasure. On the other end of the spectrum, you can trawl yard sales and vintage stores to expand your in-game collection of novelty T-shirts. In addition to a comprehensive variety of radio stations and podcasts, there are also three basic TV channels to choose from: Visit Leonida, Megamundo, and Weazel. The Spanish-language Megamundo — a parody of the real-world Telemundo — is the best of the bunch, and that's all down to one show that sunk its claws into me the second I tuned in: El Destino Extiende Sus Alas, which translates to "destiny spreads its wings."
This soap opera centers on the intense drama within a wealthy family. Patriarch Don Antonio de Ramos moves to rewrite his will to name the domestic worker Marisol as heir to his land, which sets off a war between his son and second wife as they all jostle for control over the lavish estate. El Destino Extiende Sus Alas is a parody of a well-known Colombian soap from the early 2000s called Pasión de Gavilanes, which you can watch free on Pluto TV.
After watching a really hokey fight sequence in which Don Antonio defends Marisol's honor by very slowly punching a man and then setting him on fire by tossing his cigar, I was locked in. GTA 6 kept trying to subtly pull me away from the show by zooming out from Jason and Lucia's television, wordlessly suggesting I get up and move around, maybe eat a protein bar and do some squats. No way! I had to see what happened next.
I didn't grow up speaking Spanish at home, but I studied it through middle school and high school. Watching telenovelas definitely helped me to learn the language, because I loved all the melodrama and wild twists. item.title: GTA 6 players swore the weather system was broken and the latest patch has confirmed those suspicions
item.summary: Rockstar brought weather back to Leonida.
item.text:
In my first 30 hours of Grand Theft Auto 6, I think I saw it rain once. And that was during a particularly gloomy main story mission where it felt like it was intentionally flipped on and not a serendipitous moment created by the game's weather system.
I was not alone in wondering what was up with the weather in Leonida. GTA 6 players have been confused by the lack of rain and fog since day one, especially after Rockstar boasted about the kind of storms and hurricanes it can create to Game Informer in September.
Apparently, the questioning was justified: The weather system was broken and should now be fixed in a new patch that went out today.
"Fixed an issue that resulted in weather not changing for extended periods," the patch notes say, confirming that, while some players witnessed changes in weather, it was not properly happening at the rate it was intended.
You don't partner with The Weather Channel to post exclusive pre-release screenshots of your game if the forecast is mostly sunny and not actually representative of Florida, the state with the most unpredictable weather in the US. GTA 6 has realistically detailed radio towers that left a TikTok guy who's worked on them in real life gobsmacked. It would've been bizarre if Rockstar neglected to put that kind of effort into a system normies like me would notice within a few hours.
The sun's reign is over and all the other meteorological conditions can take the spotlight. As someone who takes their time doing all the silly little daily routines in Jason and Lucia's life and abiding by traffic laws for the vibes, I'm excited to see how much the weather affects the mood. I'll just have to remember to be a little more discerning when chasing down one of GTA 6's cars to make sure I don't absolutely ruin the interior from a surprise storm.

As Grand Theft Auto 6 began releasing around the world last week, players quickly became obsessed with Mandy. She's a neighbor of Jason's who tries to seduce the himbo while he fixes her sink. [Ed. note: Light spoilers for the end of Chapter 1 and beginning of Chapter 2 follow. We'll keep them vague.]
After Jason is injured at the end of Chapter 1, Lucia takes him to a run-down motel to lie low. She wants to find stronger painkillers for him, which leads her to Vicki. She's a goth exotic dancer who also moonlights as a small-time drug dealer, and immediately pulls one over on Lucia by selling her over-the-counter Zombix (GTA's brand of painkiller) for $50. They get Vicki's paycheck from Delights Cabaret and save her friend Dunk from a gang, all the while getting to know one another. Players have quickly fallen for Vicki. "Love her she's my favorite character so far," one player wrote on Reddit.

item.title: GTA 6 Is So Unstoppable It's Even Made Nickelback Go Viral
item.summary: GTA 6 features a radio station with alternate-language covers of pop songs, the best of which is the Greek Nickelback "How You Remind Me" cover.
item.text:
It's still a debate whether Grand Theft Auto 6 has the best gaming soundtrack of 2026, but it certainly has the most soundtrack of 2026. Rockstar Games' latest open-world crime epic features more than 800 songs, most of which you'll hear on its 26 genre-themed radio stations. Of all this breadth of wild music, you'd figure the most popular song on the soundtrack would be something that had overlap with a Fast and Furious OST. But it turns out the single best song in the GTA 6 soundtrack is something by... Nickelback?
Thanks to GTA 6, Nickelback's 2001 angst ballad "How You Remind Me" has been getting a lot of play — kind of. Technically, this version is a cover. GTA 6's Kaleidoscope FM radio station plays alternate-language versions of popular songs, the indisputable best of which is "Ola Afta Poui Fovamai," by the Greek singer and alternate former tourism minister Alkistis Protopsalti. As far as covers go, this is one for the ages. Seriously, listen:
You might be somewhat surprised to hear "How You Remind Me" making the rounds again, years removed from its days reigning over the Billboard charts. To this day, the most-played radio song of the 2000s has been relegated to background music in the daddest bars from Mississauga to Massapequa. It is arguably the epitome not just of Dad Rock but specifically of Divorced Dad Rock. If "How You Remind Me" was a person, its kitchen would include Slim Jims (assorted flavors), cold pizza (definitely pepperoni), and nothing else. It would drive a 2014 Corvette Stingray (bright red, obviously). It would live on the golf course.
But with "Ola Afta Poui Fovamai," Protopsalti injects a youthful, upbeat verve to Chad Kroeger's genius composition that legendarily emerged, nearly fully formed, from his brain in just 45 minutes following an argument with a partner. There is practically zero Divorced Dad energy in "Ola Afta Poui Fovamai." It is transformational.

item.title: Every Playable Video Game in GTA 6, Ranked Worst to Best
item.summary: Grand Theft Auto 6 features four playable video games within the game. Here's how they stack up.
item.text:
Grand Theft Auto 6 is so big that it’s actually five games in one. Like previous games in the series, there are several games-within-the-game that you can play while hanging out in Leonida. These aren’t just quick arcade games that you can play for a few minutes, but full-on console games that are actually pretty fun in their own right.
It’s a playful meta joke from Rockstar, and I would be remiss not to play into it. Where there are games, there must be a video game website ranking those games in an arbitrary list. Here’s how the four games featured in GTA 6 stack up. Even if they aren’t all winners, they’re all at least high-effort jokes that deserve some praise.
As a parody of the kind of hunting games you find in dive bars, Bang For Your Buck is a pretty one-note gag. It’s an on-rails shooter where you simply have to gun down bucks while sparing does that populate three stages. The only real twist is that your money ticks down along with the timer, so you need to kill deer rapidly to keep playing. That mechanic is reused for a much better game that you’ll see higher on this list, so Bang For Your Buck doesn’t have much going for it beyond the obvious hunting satire. But as a piece of worldbuilding? It’s pure Florida, and I’m glad that it exists in Leonida.
Street Trash 3: Dezombifier is GTA 6’s very own Vampire Survivors clone. It’s a top-down twin-stick shooter where the goal is to gun through dense waves of zombies (and skeletons, for some reason) as you hunt for gears. As a send-up, it’s a little hit-and-miss. The roguelite is fun enough with its reliable choose-three level-up system, though it could have benefited from adopting Vampire Survivors’ more intuitive auto-firing action. It’s a little less effective as satire than some other entries on his list, since it feels more like a parody of AAA action games, complete with its quippy narrator. Still, it’s a fun little distraction that even has its own unlock system to keep you playing and find new weapons.
Arguably the funniest and most unexpected gag in all of GTA 6, Tenebrae Lux is Rockstar at the height of its satirical powers. The black-and-white puzzle game is a send-up of arthouse indie games created by auteur developers. "He was a tremendous admirer of Rockstar Games."
The estate of late American R&B artist D’Angelo has spoken out after the launch of GTA 6, which featured a song that he created for the game back in 2024.
GTA 6 features a slew of songs, both licensed and original, from a wide variety of high-profile music artists. Names like Cardi B, Tame Impala, Burna Boy, and many more contributed to the game’s soundtrack. D’Angelo was one of those artists who created a track for the game two years ahead of its highly anticipated November 2026 launch.
The song, titled ‘Kamikaze,’ is a funky tune that players quickly discovered during their playthroughs. Snippets of the track were uploaded to social media mere days after GTA 6’s release, and now, D’Angelo’s estate has officially confirmed the track’s existence in the game.
The track and its title were shared on November 23, 2026, in a series of Instagram posts on D’Angelo’s official profile. One of these included a statement penned by his brother, Luther Archer, who described how

The cover artwork was done by Andre Trenier, the genius brother of Michael's mentor and longtime manager Dominque Trenier.”
D’Angelo has a storied history with Rockstar; he created a song for the Red Dead Redemption 2 soundtrack titled ‘May I? Stand Unshaken,’ a collaboration that came about after he asked to playtest the game at Rockstar’s New York Offices before its release.

Here’s how to complete Crosstown Traffic in GTA 6.
The mission, which is given by your new contact Raul, splits the couple across Vice City. While Jason follows a convoy of boats along the river on a motorbike, Lucia boards a metro overground train to get close to one of the gang’s associates.
Here’s everything you need to know about completing Crosstown Traffic in GTA 6, including what rewards you’ll get at the end of it.

Guides: If you're playing Grand Theft Auto 6, make sure to check out our complete walkthrough hub, featuring beginner tips, navigation experience explained, GTA 6 cheats, and more.
Once you’ve received the phonecall from Raul, you can start the mission from either of two locations:
Starting as Lucia: Head to the Courtyard Bar in Stockyard to meet Raul.
Starting as Jason: Visit the boatyard in La Perle to meet Karim.
It doesn’t matter which character you choose. Both starting locations lead into the same mission, with the story switching between Lucia and Jason as the operation unfolds. This also doesn’t impact what rewards you get, or any choices in the mission.
The mission is split into several objectives, alternating between Lucia’s metro operation and Jason’s pursuit of the boat convoy. The game swaps you between the two automatically, so you don’t need to keep an eye on this.
After the opening cutscene, you’ll take control of Jason, who is riding a motorbike along the riverbank.
Your objective is to follow the boats carrying the shipment. Stick to the dirt paths alongside the river and keep the boats in sight as you follow it through Vice City. If you let them get away, or destroy the bike by falling into the water, the mission will end.

Lucia’s part of the mission begins with her missing the train.

item.text:
The infamous hacker who published 90 GTA VI gameplay videos before the game was officially revealed has been released from prison. Arion Kurtaj is now a free man after being a teen hacker causing cyber mayhem.
On Monday morning, the criminal was sentenced at Woolwich Crown Court following a guilty plea made last week. We reported how he plead guilty to all of his crimes including fraud, computer misuse and more.
The BBC reports Kurtaj was sentenced by the judge to 7 years in prison. However, Mr Justice Turner had him walk away free today. It is claimed the hacker smiled when the judge freed him. As part of his release, Kurtaj has been given a Serious Crime Prevention Order for 5 years. This means he is given restricted internet usage such a ban on Telegram and Discord.
This will be a surprise to some fans and worrisome given his past claims of intent to reoffend. Rockstar Games might be concerned and disappointed by this result. We got GTA VI hacker released before GTA VI Online.
“You are obviously a very talented young man. Don’t waste those talents by spending the rest of your life in and out of prison. Don’t let this happen again.” Judge Turner
Kurtaj was originally moved into a secure hospital for his own and others’ safety. Eventually, he got out and placed into a standard prison at the start of this year. We reported on some of his communication from inside his cell here.
“Arion Kurtaj used sophisticated hacking techniques to carry out a sustained campaign of cyberattacks, causing serious disruption to major international business and putting sensitive information at risk… This was an exceptionally complex and challenging case, but despite his efforts to conceal his identity online, our specialist prosecutors were able to work closely with the City of London Police and international law enforcement partners to build a strong case that exposed his actions and resulted in his guilty pleas.” Robert Hutchinson, Specialist Prosecutor, Crown Prosecution Service
Hopefully this is the end of Arion Kurtaj’s story with Rockstar Games and GTA VI. With Cyberleek still on the loose, Rockstar don’t need more interference.

Похоже, что разработчики нашли способ захватить женскую аудиторию.
Недавно состоялся релиз Grand Theft Auto VI. В игре пара главных героев, Лусия и Джейсон, и игроки могут развивать отношения между ними. Некоторых женщин это беспокоит, но порой есть и те, кого игра Rockstar Games затягивает.
Недавно пользователь под ником PorkPoncho рассказал, что его жена начала играть в Grand Theft Auto VI. Он теперь за этим наблюдает и делится её успехами: «Рассказываю про приключения моей жены в GTA VI — она уже практически забрала игру себе, чтобы свободно гулять по миру за Лусию».
Позвала Джейсона погулять и потащила его по магазинам, чтобы принарядить.
Сходила с ним поесть и украла у него картошку фри.
Вместе с ним ограбила ломбард — оба были в своих «милых нарядах».
И затем снова потащила Джейсона по магазинам, чтобы обновить им обоим гардероб, а потом поиграла в мини-гольф (Джейсон выиграл).
После этого она отправилась в поход. PorkPoncho спросил «это отдельная активность в игре или она просто гуляла?» — ответила, что «припарковалась в красивом месте и пошла бродить». Позднее она призналась, что весь этот поход затевался ради поиска красивого вида, на фоне которого Джейсон мог бы фотографить Лусию в её милом наряде.
Приключения геймерши продолжаются. По словам PorkPoncho, она «просто помешалась на симуляторной составляющей игры», для неё это лучше, чем The Sims:

item.title: Sony Touts Nearly 40 Million GTA 6 Players on PS5
item.summary: Four days removed from launch, Sony is already reporting insane player numbers for GTA 6. As is stands, nearly 40 million have jumped in. The post Sony Touts Nearly 40 Million GTA 6 Players on PS5 appeared first on Insider Gaming .
item.text:
It’s already been a whirlwind for GTA 6 since it launched just last Thursday. Since then, Rockstar’s new masterpiece has been rated #1 all-time by critics, review-bombed by certain players, and everything in between.
Turns out overall, however, the game seems to be doing incredibly well. New data shared by Sony shows that in the last four days, nearly 40 million unique players have decided to jump into GTA 6 on PS5.
You can purchase Grand Theft Auto 6 here if you want to see what all the hype is about.
A few days ago, GTA 6 publisher Take-Two Interactive already claimed that the game had sold over 32 million units. Today, information provided by Sony shows that the actual current player base has moved several million beyond that number on PS5 consoles alone.
In a post on PlayStation Blog, Sony mentions that GTA 6 has been the largest single-game launch in the history of PlayStation across all generations. At the time of their story going live, over 39 million unique players had started the game. It’s important to note that the number of “unique players” does not directly correlate to the total number of sales, but it’s still an insane player count regardless.
Further fleshing out this staggering number of players, it’s also claimed that 683 million collective hours of GTA 6 have been played by these 39 million users on PS5, which averages out to about 17.4 hours per person since November 19.
PS Blog also states that GTA 6 broke the record for the title with the most concurrent players at once on PlayStation, and 70% of new consoles purchased since the game came out booted up GTA 6 before anything else.
We’ve yet to see Xbox report on player count stats for GTA 6 since launch, but whatever the number of players on the Microsoft console is, combined with PS5’s 39 million+, is sure to be even more staggering.

item.title: Sony: GTA 6 set record for 'highest number of concurrent players for any game on PlayStation' ever
item.summary: The industry is finding new milestones to measure GTA 6's success.
item.text:
GTA 6 has been shattering records since before it came out, becoming the top-rated game in the history of Metacritic before it had the biggest entertainment launch (by dollars) in history. Sony is now joining in that victory lap by sharing GTA 6 milestones as they pertain to PlayStation.
"More than 39 million unique players have experienced Jason and Lucia's story in Grand Theft Auto 6 on PlayStation 5," Sony content communications manager Tim Turi wrote in a blog post today. That is a staggering number, especially considering GTA 6 also launched on Xbox and will (eventually) hit PC.
But that's not a sales record—Rockstar still has a ways to go to surpass GTA 5's 230 million lifetime sales. What is unprecedented, at least for PlayStation, is GTA 6's concurrents over launch weekend.
"GTA 6 set a new record for the highest number of concurrent players for any game on PlayStation, surpassing previous records across multiplayer, free-to-play, and single-player titles," Turi said.
That's the wild one to me, because that means more people were playing GTA 6 at the same time on the largest console platform than Call of Duty, GTA 5, or even Fortnite has ever achieved. Turi didn't share the concurrent figure itself, which is too bad—Steam remains the only platform that hands out exact player data. If the figure is theoretically higher than some of the biggest concurrent peaks we know about on Steam, then it could've been as high as 3-4 million players.

Now that the dust has somewhat settled after the avalanche that was the launch of GTA 6, PlayStation has revealed some of its stats from the game, revealing that this was the single largest game release in PlayStation history.
PlayStation’s November 23 blog post states that more than 39 million unique players have played the game on the PlayStation 5, setting a new record for the highest number of concurrent players for any PlayStation game. This beats out other records for multiplayer games, single-player games, and perhaps most astonishingly, even free-to-play titles.
On top of that, GTA 6 players logged a total of 683 million hours played in the game, with the average player spending an estimated 17.4 hours sticking up virtual pawn shops and stealing NPC’s cars during its first few days.
What’s more impressive is the sheer amount of people who purchased PS5s specifically to play GTA 6. PlayStation’s blog says it saw the “largest number of newly-connected PS5 consoles on a single day” since the console’s launch in November 2020, not counting end-of-year holidays like Christmas. Since GTA 6’s launch, it was the first game played on 70% of these new consoles.
GTA 6 has, perhaps unsurprisingly, broken a slew of big records. The most prominent of these is its status as the biggest entertainment launch of all time, with Rockstar reporting that the game earned $3.79 billion in its first 24 hours.

item.text:
Just about every veteran developer in the industry has been heaping praise on GTA 6 since its release last week, but I'm not sure any of that rampant positivity matches the thoughts of Igor Sarzynski.
Sarzynski is currently the creative director on Cyberpunk 2 (as it's officially known right now), having previously worked on both The Witcher 3 and Cyberpunk 2077 — two games that are widely considered to be amongst the best that the open world genre has to offer.
In other words, Sarzynski knows what he's talking about when he says GTA 6 is "probably the single greatest artistic achievement in history". Now that's praise.
"GTA 6-induced-open-world-game-dev-depression is real," he noted on social media.
"Probably the single greatest artistic achievement in history, I mean it. Scale, density, coherence, thoughtfulness of it all, just a technological and creative miracle."
"Cyberpunk 2 is cancelled," Sarzynski jokes, suggesting that no one's going to match Rockstar's effort for quite some time. "I'mma go sweep autumn leaves in my backyard now."
If you've played GTA 6, you can surely understand why every non-Rockstar developer is looking at it and being left in a state of near disbelief. We're not getting another release like it for years and years to come — and just like Red Dead Redemption 2 before it, it's going to become the benchmark for open world games.
Still, there'll come a time when Cyberpunk 2 takes all the headlines — it's just that right now, it's hard to see beyond GTA 6 because it's absolutely bloody everywhere (and with good reason).
"Seriously though I think we're doing something of our own, with a different unique flavour," Sarzynski continues in a follow-up post.
"GTA is impressive in a way all great art is, it expands what is possible, a captivating vision flawlessly executed," he concludes — and that's pretty much a perfect way to put it.

item.text:
One of Grand Theft Auto 6’s strangest random encounters occurs when you’re offering taxi services, and a man with a beard wearing a dark suit and sunglasses climbs into the backseat with a gun. This can happen if you’re playing as either Jason or Lucia, but both scenes play out the same way: The man wants you to run a red light, ignore phone calls, and drive him to Harborside Park in Vice Beach. He also sounds an awful lot like Tom Cruise, with a calm but forceful demeanor that seems almost sociopathic. Several clips of the sequence have already hit the internet, and to many people, it’s an obvious nod to Collateral, Michael Mann’s 2004 thriller about a hitman who takes a cab driver hostage.
Jason or Lucia gets a better deal than Mann’s cabbie in this Easter egg. If you take the stranger to his destination and follow him inside after he takes out some of the criminals there, you can find a ton of valuable loot. Most players seem keen on eliminating the stranger rather than keep driving him around. In Collateral, Jamie Foxx’s character, Max, has to spend the whole night driving Cruise’s Vincent around Los Angeles. If you’ve never seen how that goes for him, Collateral is streaming for free on Pluto TV — and it’s a must-watch, especially if you want a movie that has a vibe as wild and crime-filled as GTA 6’s.
Max is a cab driver who’s been telling himself for years that the job is temporary. He wants to start his own limo company someday, so when a well-dressed passenger named Vincent (Cruise) offers him $600 to drive him around for the night, it seems like the kind of opportunity that could get him a little closer to quitting. Then a body lands on his cab at their first destination. Vincent has five people to kill before the night is over. Max has just agreed to drive him to all five stops — and he’s already an accomplice.
Vincent is one of Cruise’s best roles because so much of what makes him convincing as an action hero makes him downright scary here. The same certainty that lets Ethan Hunt talk somebody into jumping out of a plane makes it seem perfectly reasonable, for about half a second, when Vincent asks Max to help him stuff a body in the trunk. He’s also an obnoxious backseat driver. The longer he spends in the cab, the more interested he becomes in why Max has seemingly wasted so much of his life. Some of his advice is irritatingly solid, yet he’s also a man who could end the conversation with a single gunshot whenever he wanted to.
